## Measurement: the enterprise `organization_id` stamper gap

Measured against `origin/main` at `50cf2940b9` (worktree `objectstack-issue-13497`, detached, nothing edited). Pure measurement per the card — no code change, no PR, no priority label touched.

---

## 0. FIRST — the look-back clause IS triggered

> **回头条款**:若测量发现**系统(isSystem)写入**也存在落 NULL 租户行的真实路径,#13491 的「isSystem 出范围」裁定回决策箱重裁。

**Such a path exists, it is not hypothetical, and the repository's own test suite pins it.**

`packages/objectql/src/system-write-organization.test.ts` contains, as a passing assertion:

> `'a platform-namespace object stays org-less on the %s posture'` — `it.each(['isolated', 'single'])` — asserting `lastWrite(observed, 'sys_audit_entry').options.tenantId` is `undefined`.

`isolated` is a **walled** posture. So on a walled deployment an `isSystem` insert on a platform-namespace object reaches the driver with no tenant, `injectTenantOnInsert` stamps nothing, and the row lands `organization_id = NULL` — with the `[tenant-audit]` warning explicitly silenced by the same `isSystem` flag.

Executed, not merely read: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/system-write-organization.test.ts` gives `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 20 passed (20)`. The same file's **refusal** tests (`#8844 multi-organization — the write is REFUSED, never defaulted`, `it.each(['isolated','group'])`) pass in that same run, so the probe discriminates: it is not answering "undefined" for everything.

The chain, link by link, all in shipped source:

1. `SYSTEM_CTX` is `{ isSystem: true }` — **no `tenantId`** — in 20+ separate definitions across the tree (`packages/services/service-queue/src/common.ts:27`, `packages/services/service-job/src/db-job-adapter.ts:16`, `packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-lifecycle.ts:88`, and so on).
2. `ObjectQLEngine.buildDriverOptions` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:3543`): `hasTenant` is false, so no `opts.tenantId`; `isSystem` sets `opts.bypassTenantAudit = true`.
3. `SqlDriver.injectTenantOnInsert` (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts:11944`): returns immediately when `tenantId` is empty — **nothing is stamped**.
4. `SqlDriver.auditMissingTenant` (`:11968`): returns immediately on `bypassTenantAudit` — **nothing is reported**.
5. The one mechanism that would otherwise catch this, `ObjectQLEngine.resolveSystemInsertOrganization` (`engine.ts:3754`), returns `undefined` at its second guard: `if (isPlatformNamespaceObject(object)) return undefined;`.

**Why this is more than a re-statement of "unscoped by design".** The `sys_` / `cloud_` / `ai_` carve-out is justified in `packages/objectql/src/tenancy/system-write-organization.ts:66-77` by #8672's reasoning that "an org-less row is defensible for `sys_permission_set`". But the tree simultaneously treats a number of `sys_*` objects as genuinely tenant-scoped, and has been repairing them one door at a time:

- `sys_file` — insert door repaired #12745; update/delete doors repaired #13178 (landed today, `f087c376ff`);
- `sys_upload_session` — insert door repaired #12928; update/delete doors repaired #13178;
- `sys_http_delivery` — `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-outbox-plugin.ts:364` says in as many words: "`sys_http_delivery` is tenant-scoped, and this is the one door on it a request can reach: an unscoped replay from here is an authenticated user reaching another organization's delivery row on a walled deployment";
- `sys_notification_delivery` — organization stamping added #11698.

Four objects, four separate repairs, all inside a namespace that the only class-level enforcement excludes wholesale. The blanket exclusion and the per-object repairs cannot both be right. That is the decision this puts back in the box, and it is a stronger statement than "isSystem is unscoped by design" — the design **has** an enforcement point, and the namespace rule routes exactly the contested objects around it.

---

## 1. The boundary — stated as a boundary, not as a gap in effort

**1a. Middleware A is out of tree.** Confirmed. This session's repository scope is `objectstack-ai/objectstack` and `objectstack-ai/objectui`; the enterprise middleware is in neither, so its stamp conditions cannot be read. Nothing below asserts what it does.

**1b. #13178's census comment is UNREACHABLE.** `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/13178` returns **404** on three independent channels — unauthenticated REST, the rendered web page, and authenticated MCP `issue_read`. Positive control on the same channels in the same minute: #13497 → 200, #13491 → 200, #13179 → 200. So the 404 is about that number, not a broken channel.

⇒ **The canonical list of 24 could be neither copied nor verified.** Everything below is an independent re-derivation from the tree, with its criterion stated. The census's *summary* survives in-tree, in the changeset the #13178 repair landed (`.changeset/tenant-audit-update-delete-half-repairs.md`, now merged):

> "The tenant-audit census counted 175 service write call sites against a tenancy-enabled object, 24 of them carrying no tenant context at all"

**Corroboration that the re-derivation is measuring the same family** (this matters, because the exact list is gone):

| census figure (from #13491 / the changeset) | re-derived here |
|---|---|
| 175 write call sites, of which 127 statically decidable | 132 literal-object engine write call sites |
| 48 runtime-parameter-name sites (a gate is structurally blind to them) | 479 dynamic-name write calls overall; 152 on an engine-typed receiver |
| 135 silenced by the `isSystem` guard before the posture gate | **141** sites carrying an `isSystem`/seed context |
| 24 carrying no tenant context at all | **29** engine write sites with no tenant channel in the call |

The 127 vs 132 and 135 vs 141 agreements are close enough to establish the same population; the differences are line rot, the four doors repaired since, and my scanner's own limits (below). **I am not claiming to have reproduced "the 24".**

**1c. What a purely textual re-derivation cannot decide** — measured on myself, twice:
- an argument list longer than my capture window read as "no context" when `{ context: SYSTEM_CTX }` sat past the cut (`file-reference-lifecycle.ts:363`, `db-job-adapter.ts:497`);
- a tenant threaded through a variable (`...options`, `...scope`, a `row` built above the call) is invisible to the call-site text (`sql-http-outbox.ts:393` **does** carry `{ tenantId }` via `...scope`; `sql-outbox.ts:121` **does** carry `organization_id` on its row).

Every site named below was hand-read in full after the scan. This limitation is itself the evidence for #13491's recorded finding that a CI gate can judge only 127/175.

---

## 2. Output 1 — Middleware A's stamp conditions and coverage

Not readable directly. What **is** measurable is the complete set of seams through which any tenant value can reach a write — which bounds what any middleware, in tree or out, can do.

**There are exactly four channels, and every one of them is explicit at the call site:**

| # | Channel | Where | Applies to |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ExecutionContext.tenantId`, passed as `context` | `buildDriverOptions`, `engine.ts:3567` | all write ops |
| 2 | `DriverOptions.tenantId`, passed directly in the options bag | preserved by `buildDriverOptions` (it only fills `opts.tenantId` when `undefined`); used this way by `sql-http-outbox.redeliver` | all write ops |
| 3 | the tenant column set on the row payload | `injectTenantOnInsert` never overwrites an explicit value | insert only |
| 4 | the engine's own derivation, `resolveSystemInsertOrganization` | `engine.ts:9383`, inside `insert()` | insert only, application objects only |

**There is NO ambient channel.** The engine's only `AsyncLocalStorage` is `txStore` (`engine.ts:2225`) and it carries `transaction` and `scope` — no tenant. Control that fired: the probe for ambient stores *did* find one, so it is capable of finding another; there is no second. And the injected column carries no database default — `TENANT_SCOPE_FIELD_DEF` (`packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts:105`) is `{ type: 'lookup', reference: 'sys_organization', label, required: false, hidden: true, readonly: true, system: true, description }`, with no `defaultValue`, while sibling injected defs in the same module do carry other keys.

**Consequence, and it needs no out-of-tree reading.** An HTTP middleware can reach a write only by (1)/(2)/(3) *at the call site*, or by acting below the platform (a column DEFAULT, a trigger, RLS). For a call site that constructs its own row and passes no context — which is precisely the population in question — the first three are unavailable to it, because the middleware never sees that payload and there is no ambient slot to fill. Whether the enterprise deployment closes the gap **below** the platform is out of tree and is a 判不了.

**And the question is narrower than it looks, because the engine already refuses most of it.** `resolveSystemInsertOrganization` (#8844, maintainer ruling 2026-08-15) runs on **every** insert lacking a context tenant, not only `isSystem` ones — its first guard is `carriesOrganization(execCtx?.tenantId)`, not `isSystem`. On a walled posture it **throws** `SystemWriteOrganizationRequiredError` (`code: 'ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED'`, `status: 500`) rather than landing a NULL row. Its three exclusions are: objects with no tenant column / `tenancy.enabled: false` / federated; **the `sys_` / `cloud_` / `ai_` namespace**; and writes already carrying an organization. It is **INSERT-only**, deliberately.

⇒ For **application** objects on a walled deployment, the stamper question is moot: an unscoped insert is refused, not stamped-or-NULLed. **The entire residual NULL-tenant exposure sits in the platform namespace and on update/delete** — and platform-namespace rows are exactly what an HTTP middleware is least placed to stamp, because they are written by services from their own payloads.

---

## 3. Output 2 — the sites, classified one by one

Population re-derived as: write calls (`insert`/`insertMany`/`update`/`delete`/`upsert`/`bulkCreate`/`bulkDelete`/`updateMany`/`deleteMany`) on an engine-typed receiver, in shipped `packages/**` source (tests, benchmarks, `packages/verify` harness, MCP bridge and spec migration doc-strings excluded), on an object whose tenant field resolves.

Object-level facts used: `managedBy: 'better-auth'` suppresses the injected column entirely (`resolveInjectedSystemColumns`, `packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-columns.ts:156`), so `sys_user` / `sys_session` / `sys_account` / `sys_oauth_application` / `sys_two_factor` are **outside** the population; `sys_member` and `sys_invitation` are **inside** it because they declare `organization_id` themselves. `sys_api_key` and `sys_sso_provider` declare `tenancy: { enabled: false }` and are outside.

### 3A. NOT COVERABLE by an HTTP middleware — reachable only by a non-HTTP entry path

A site reachable only this way cannot be covered whatever Middleware A does. This needs no out-of-tree reading and is the firmest thing here.

| Site | Object | Op | Entry path |
|---|---|---|---|
| `packages/cli/src/commands/secret/orphans.ts:396` | `sys_secret` | delete | oclif CLI command; boots its own schema stack in-process (`bootSchemaStack`) and calls the **driver** directly (`deleting.delete`), bypassing the engine and `buildDriverOptions` entirely. No HTTP server in the process. |
| `packages/services/service-job/src/db-job-adapter.ts:497` | `sys_job` | update | `bumpJob`, the scheduler's post-run counter write. Carries `SYSTEM_CTX`. |
| `packages/services/service-messaging/src/sql-http-outbox.ts:319` | `sys_http_delivery` | update | `ack`, the dispatcher sweep. Already classified as a dispatcher sweep by #11010. |
| `packages/services/service-messaging/src/sql-outbox.ts:300` | `sys_notification_delivery` | update | `ack`, dispatcher sweep; `dispatcherAckCasOptions` sets `bypassTenantAudit: true` deliberately (#11010). |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/migrate-webhook-secrets.ts:115` | webhook subscriptions object (runtime arg) | update | Plugin **boot sweep**, called from `webhook-outbox-plugin.ts:265` during plugin start. Carries `SYSTEM_CTX`. |
| `packages/services/service-storage/src/backfill-file-references.ts:186` | `sys_file` | insert | Backfill pass. Carries `SYSTEM_CTX`; the file contains **no** `organization_id` reference at all. |

### 3B. NOT COVERABLE — HTTP can trigger it, but the write leaves the request path, and no organization channel exists to carry

| Site | Object | Op | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `packages/services/service-messaging/src/sql-http-outbox.ts:178` | `sys_http_delivery` | insert | **`EnqueueHttpInput` has no `organizationId` member at all** — grep for it in `packages/services/service-messaging/src/http-outbox.ts` returns nothing, while the sibling `EnqueueDeliveryInput` in `sql-outbox.ts` *does* have one (`:37`, `:80`, the #11698 repair). So no caller can supply an organization even if it has one. Producers: the automation HTTP node (`service-automation/src/builtin/http-nodes.ts:125`) and the webhook auto-enqueuer, which `webhook-outbox-plugin.ts:86` documents as running "fire-and-forget (off the write path)". |
| `packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.ts:363` | `sys_file` | insert | `copyOwnedFile`, an engine lifecycle hook, fires for HTTP-originated and background-originated writes alike. Carries `{ context: { ...SYSTEM_CTX } }`; the file contains **no** `organization_id` reference. This is the create door #12745 repaired, reached by a second path that does not go through `StorageMetadataStore`. |

**`sys_http_delivery` deserves calling out on its own.** Every row this object gets is enqueued through `:178` with `organization_id = NULL`. The driver's tenant term is `(organization_id = :tenantId OR organization_id IS NULL)` (`sql-driver.ts:11931`, #2734's deliberate global-row fail-open). So the #10740 wall on `redeliver` — which correctly threads the caller's active organization to stop "an authenticated user reaching another organization's delivery row on a walled deployment" — is reachable around for **100% of rows**, because 100% of them are NULL-tenant. The scoping repair and the enqueue gap are in the same file, 200 lines apart.

### 3C. Both HTTP and non-HTTP entry — an HTTP middleware could cover at most the HTTP half

| Site | Object | Op | Entry paths |
|---|---|---|---|
| `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:17672` | `sys_metadata` | update | `reassignOrphanedMetadata`; metadata protocol, served over HTTP and driven by CLI push and boot-time package install |
| `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:17726` | `sys_metadata_commit` | insert | `persistPackageCommitRow`; same |
| `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:19429` | `sys_metadata` | delete | `deleteMetaItem`; same |
| `packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts:103` | `sys_metadata` | insert | `persistDatasourceRow`; admin routes plus programmatic registration |
| `packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts:121` | `sys_metadata` | delete | `deleteDatasourceRow`; same |
| `packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-secret-binder.ts:100` | `sys_secret` | insert | `bind`; datasource credential binding, admin route plus boot registration |
| `packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-secret-binder.ts:115` | `sys_secret` | delete | `unbind`; same |
| `packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service-plugin.ts:317` | `sys_secret` | insert | settings store; passes `{ bypassTenantAudit: true }` — no tenant, and the report is silenced without an `isSystem` context |
| `packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service-plugin.ts:335` | `sys_secret` | update | same |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/adopt-membership.ts:230` | `sys_member` | update | `adoptExistingMembership`, from the better-auth adapter's create door; HTTP auth routes plus server-side `auth.api` calls |

### 3D. 判不了 — cannot determine, with the reason for each

| Site(s) | Reason it cannot be determined |
|---|---|
| `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts` — `:859`, `:975`, `:996`, `:1015`, `:1031`, `:1048`, `:1079`, `:1119`, `:1149`, `:1162`, `:1172`, `:1180` (12 sites) | **The object is a runtime parameter** (`objectName`, resolved from a better-auth model name). Most better-auth models carry no tenant column at all (`managedBy: 'better-auth'` suppresses the injection) and are therefore outside the population; `sys_member` and `sys_invitation` declare `organization_id` themselves and are inside it. Which of the two a given call is depends on the model at runtime. This is exactly #13491's "48 runtime-parameter-name sites, structurally blind". |
| `packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts:272`, `:286`, `:293` | Object is a runtime parameter (`table`). Additionally the class has an **engine-or-driver fork**: with no engine it calls `this.driver.create/update/delete` directly, bypassing `buildDriverOptions` and the audit entirely. It *does* have a tenant channel of its own — a constructor-level `organizationId` conditionally stamped at `:1218` — so whether a given write carries an organization depends on how the loader was constructed. |
| Every question of the form "does Middleware A stamp this one" | **Out of tree.** Not readable, and answering it would be invention rather than measurement. |
| Whether a walled enterprise deployment closes the gap **below** the platform — a column DEFAULT, an insert trigger, or RLS on `organization_id` | Out of tree. In-tree the column is declared with no default and nothing writes one. |

### 3E. Population II — `isSystem` writes on tenancy-enabled platform objects

Not part of "the 24" (these are the 135 the `isSystem` guard silences), but the look-back clause is about them, so they are measured here.

**141** engine write sites carry an `isSystem`/seed context. Of the 87 with a statically resolvable object name, **66** target a tenancy-enabled platform-namespace object; **49** of those carry no tenant value anywhere in the call; **13** of those are inserts, i.e. writes that land a fresh NULL-tenant row. Hand-verified as carrying no organization on any path (the whole file contains no `organization_id` reference):

- `packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.ts:363` — `sys_file`
- `packages/services/service-storage/src/backfill-file-references.ts:186` — `sys_file`
- `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-service.ts:518` — `sys_share_link`
- `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts:1232` — `sys_record_share`
- `packages/plugins/plugin-reports/src/report-service.ts:433` — `sys_saved_report`
- `packages/plugins/plugin-reports/src/report-service.ts:635` — `sys_report_schedule`

The remaining inserts in that bucket (`sys_audit_log` from `auth-event-audit.ts:228`, `read-audit.ts:460`, `config-change-audit.ts:199`; `sys_approval_request` from `approval-service.ts:2212`) **do** stamp `organization_id` from a resolved tenant on the row — for example `auth-event-audit.ts:265` (`row.organization_id = tenantId`) and `config-change-audit.ts:197` (`row.organization_id = entry.tenantId ?? null`), both guarded on the column actually existing. They are the counter-example that shows the tree already knows how to do this on `sys_*` objects, which is why the six above read as gaps rather than as design.

A further **36** update/delete sites in the same bucket carry no tenant. Those do not create a NULL row, but they are an unscoped **reach** on a walled deployment; most are id-pinned by their `where`, which bounds the harm without removing it.

---

## 4. Output 3 — severity recommendation

⛔ **No priority label was changed by this card.** This is a recommendation back to the batch.

**For #13178's repair family: keep p1. Do not downgrade to p3.**

The p3 case required the stamper to close the gap for **all 24** sites. It does not, and this can be said without reading Middleware A:

1. Six sites (3A) are reachable **only** by CLI, scheduler, dispatcher sweep, plugin boot sweep or backfill. No HTTP middleware is in the call chain at all.
2. Two sites (3B) are HTTP-triggerable but write off the request path, and for `sys_http_delivery` the input type carries **no organization member at all** — there is nothing for a middleware to populate. Every row of that object is NULL-tenant, which reaches around a wall the platform deliberately built on the same object.
3. There is **no ambient tenant channel** in the platform. All four seams are explicit at the call site, so a middleware cannot supply a tenant to a call site that passes none.
4. The one thing that would make "no tenant context" harmless — the #8844 refusal — is **structurally excluded** from the entire `sys_` namespace, which is where essentially all of these sites write.

**Suggested grading of what remains:**

- **p1** — `sys_http_delivery` enqueue (`sql-http-outbox.ts:178`). Not hygiene: it defeats an existing, deliberate cross-organization wall on the same object, for 100% of rows, on walled deployments. Worth its own card whatever happens to the rest.
- **p1** — the `sys_file` NULL-tenant insert paths (`file-reference-lifecycle.ts:363`, `backfill-file-references.ts:186`). Same object #12745 / #12928 / #13178 have been repairing across four doors; these two doors write the same object unstamped.
- **p2** — `sys_share_link`, `sys_record_share`, `sys_saved_report`, `sys_report_schedule` inserts (3E). Sharing and reporting rows landing org-less on a walled install; harm is real but bounded by the layers above.
- **p3** — the CLI / scheduler / dispatcher / boot-sweep sites (3A), the settings `sys_secret` doors, and the metadata-protocol doors. These are the hygiene half: single-tenant-normal, id-pinned, or operator-initiated.

**For #13491's ruled scoping: the look-back clause fires — send it back.** The ruling scoped `isSystem` writes out of the control on the strength of "unscoped by design". The measurement says the design *does* have an enforcement point (#8844's refusal), that it deliberately excludes the whole `sys_` namespace, and that at least four objects inside that namespace have needed per-door tenant repairs in the last weeks. The question worth re-deciding is not "is `isSystem` in scope" but **"is the `sys_`/`cloud_`/`ai_` namespace regexp the right boundary for the #8844 exclusion, or should tenancy be declared per object (ADR-0066's `tenancy: { enabled: false }`) as the module's own header argues for the neighbouring case?"** The module already says a per-write bypass flag is the wrong shape and a per-object declaration is the right one; the namespace regexp is a per-write bypass wearing a different hat.

---

## 5. What was NOT measured

- **Middleware A itself** — out of tree. Nothing above asserts its behaviour.
- **Any below-the-platform stamping** in a walled enterprise deployment (column DEFAULT, insert trigger, RLS). Out of tree; in-tree the column has no default.
- **A per-site resolution of the 12 `objectql-adapter` sites and the 3 `database-loader` sites** — their object is a runtime parameter. Recorded as 判不了, not folded into any count.
- **A byte-exact reproduction of "the 24"** — the census is unreachable (404). The re-derivation agrees with the census summary on 127-vs-132 and 135-vs-141 but is not the same list.
- **The full gate farm** — this card changes no code, so no gate is owed. The only suite executed was the #8844 pin (20/20 pass), as a control on the central claim.
